_comment: SYNTHETIC DOCUMENTATION FIXTURE. Companion to t905-2025-layout.json.
Trench T905 is invented; so are its loci, its surfaces and its finds.
None of it is archaeological evidence.
Eight loci, each with every vertex, elevation, Munsell value and
stratigraphic assertion a real locus record carries -- and with the same
kinds of defect. Where two of T905's records are made to disagree, BOTH
readings are kept and the disagreement is named in _known_problems, which
is the practice the real thing demands. Where a record is blank, the field
Grid coordinates are signed: South and West negative. A trench book writes
'153E/22S'; that is (153.0, -22.0) here. Elevations are metres above sea
level on the corrected 25.23 mAE datum.

loci.summary: Topsoil, excavated together with the spoil heap of an earlier season
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
closing_note: These are the day-8 daily closing readings, the last full labelled set
before Locus 1 closed. The surface AS AT CLOSURE on day 9 is recorded
in the trench book as Locus 2's opening, not as Locus 1's closing. The
two sets are one physical surface read a day apart, which is what
makes them useful: see the repeatability note in _known_problems.
note: Covers only the ground not dug in the previous season. The
northeastern quadrant is not in it, which is why its eastern reading
is at 151E/20S rather than at the trench's own NE corner at 155E/20S.

loci.summary: Dark olive brown deposit between the topsoil and the Structure A features
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
closing_note: The closing list has six further readings written with no point label
and no coordinates. They sit between NE and A in the book, which is
where the six intermediate points of the opening list sit, so they
were probably taken at the same six points in the same order.
PROBABLY is not a provenance. They are kept here as bare numbers and
are given no coordinates, which is what the record supports.

loci.summary: The compacted earthen floor surface of Structure A
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
note: Left in situ as the exposed floor of Structure A, so most vertices
read the same at opening and at closing. Only the 2 x 1 m sounding
(Locus 6) cut through it. That redundancy is what makes point A's
mistyped coordinate recoverable: it is written '151E/22.58E' at
opening and '151E/32.58S' at closing, and neither is a point in this
trench, but the Locus 2 lists give 151E/22.58S at the same place
twice.

loci.summary: The western foundation wall of Structure A, preserved in a single course
loci.munsell: 10YR 3/2 very dark greyish brown (soil); 10YR 8/2 very pale brown (stones)
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement
note: Not excavated: defined, drawn, photographed and left standing. The
opening and closing readings are the same stone tops measured twice,
two weeks apart, so their differences measure the reading rather than
the excavation. They span -0.09 m to +0.05 m.

loci.summary: Cobbled exterior surface west of the Structure A wall
loci.vertex_source: daily log only; the locus form's coordinate table is blank
note: Not excavated. Its SW vertex is written '150E/26.82S' in the opening
list, which is 1.82 m south of the trench's own south baulk. The
closing list writes the same point '150E/21.82S' with the same
elevation, and Locus 3's NW is 150E/21.82S at 24.02 in both lists. The
opening entry is a digit transposition; 21.82S is used here.

loci.summary: The 2 x 1 m sounding through the Structure A floor; the same deposit as Locus 3
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement
note: Placed one metre in from the east baulk and one metre in from the
south baulk, immediately east of the Locus 4 wall, to section the
floor without destroying the exposed surface.

loci.summary: Olive brown deposit immediately beneath the Structure A floor
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement

loci.summary: Light olive brown deposit at the base of the sounding; left unexcavated
loci.vertex_source: locus form AND daily log, in exact agreement
note: Defined and left unexcavated at the end of the season. Its opening
and closing elevations are identical at all four corners, which is
what an unexcavated locus should look like and is worth checking.

relations.evidence: Locus 2 lies below Locus 1 across the whole trench; Locus 2 was opened at Locus 1's closing surface
Locus 2 underlies the topsoil and overlies the Structure A features; Locus 3's SU form gives previous loci 1, 2
Locus 5 was revealed by the removal of Locus 2; the season's drawn matrix places 5 directly below 2
Locus 6's SU form: OVERLIES Loci 7, 8. Locus 7 was opened at Locus 6's closing surface

relations.note: Redundant: it follows from 6 -> 7 -> 8. Kept because the form asserts it; the renderer drops it from the diagram and warns.

relations.evidence: A soil change at the base of Locus 7 prompted a new locus; Locus 8 was opened at Locus 7's closing surface

correlations.evidence: Locus 3's SU form: EQUAL TO Locus 6. Locus 6's SU form: EQUAL TO Locus 3. Both descriptions: Locus 6 was opened as a sounding to excavate through the floor surface of Structure A
correlations.note: Locus 6 is the part of Locus 3's deposit that was dug away. Same deposit, two numbers, because it was excavated on a different date.

abutments.record: Locus 3 SU form: IS BOUND TO Loci 4, 5
Locus 3 SU form: IS BOUND TO Loci 4, 5
Locus 6 SU form: IS BOUND TO Locus 4

abutment_note: 'IS BOUND TO' asserts that two units abut -- a claim about
contemporaneity, not about which is younger. Every edge in the Harris
schema is younger-to-older, and a correlation asserts sameness rather
than contact, so these three assertions have NO representation in the
matrix. They are recorded here so that the loss is visible instead of

vertices_and_elevations.record: invented, in the form of a trench book's daily log entries
note: Page numbers are trench book pages. Loci 4, 6, 7 and 8 additionally
have their coordinates filled in on their locus forms, and in all four
cases the two records agree to the centimetre. Loci 1, 2, 3 and 5 have
blank coordinate tables on their forms, which is the commoner state.

munsell.record: invented, in the form of daily entries and SU forms

dimensions.record: invented, in the form of SU form DIMENSIONS and STATE OF CONSERVATION fields

materials.record: invented, in the form of a season's Bone, Lithics, Metals, Slag and Pottery summaries and a Bulk Finds Chart
note: The per-locus pottery figures sum to 1,600 sherds, which is the total
the notional chart gives -- a consistency the real documents do not
always have.

stratigraphy.record: invented, in the form of SU forms, a drawn season matrix, and the daily entries at each locus change
note: Taken from OVERLIES / UNDERLIES / EQUAL TO, cross-checked against the
drawn matrix and the daily entries. The forms' PREVIOUS LOCI and
FOLLOWING LOCI columns are NOT used -- see _known_problems.

_known_problems: THE SU FORMS USE 'PREVIOUS' AND 'FOLLOWING' IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Locus
3's form gives previous loci 1, 2 and following loci 8, 7 -- previous
meaning stratigraphically above, that is, later. Locus 4's form gives
previous loci 6, 7, 8 and following loci 1, 2, exactly the reverse. Locus
6's form follows Locus 4's convention. Read literally, the two conventions
together make a cycle. Only OVERLIES, UNDERLIES and EQUAL TO are used
here, and those are consistent across every form.
LOCUS 6 IS ASSERTED TO OVERLIE BOTH 7 AND 8. Since 7 overlies 8, the 6-8
edge follows from the 6-7-8 path. It is kept in the fixture because the
form asserts it, and the transitive reduction drops it from the rendered
diagram with a redundant-relation warning. This is the documented
behaviour, exercised by a form that behaves the way forms do.
THE DRAWN MATRIX AND THE SU FORMS DISAGREE ABOUT LOCI 3 AND 6. The season
matrix stacks Locus 6 one level below Locus 3, as though 3 were younger.
Both SU forms say EQUAL TO. The forms are right and the drawing is a
drafting convenience: Locus 6 is the piece of Locus 3 that was dug
through, so it cannot be younger than itself. Encoded here as a
correlation, which is what the schema has for exactly this case.
FOUR OF EIGHT LOCUS FORMS HAVE BLANK COORDINATE TABLES (loci 1, 2, 3, 5),
and the Date Opened, Date Closed and Munsell fields are blank on the forms
for loci 1 to 5. The season's tracking spreadsheet nonetheless records this
trench as 'Locus Forms complete? Yes'. The missing values all exist in the
daily log, so nothing is lost -- but a completeness flag is not a reliable
indicator of what a form contains.
THE SU FORM CERAMIC COUNTS DO NOT MATCH THE POTTERY CHART. Locus 3's form
reports 238 ceramic fragments against the chart's 221; Locus 6's reports
437 against 436. The chart is itemised by fabric and part and is used here.
LOCUS 6'S BONE WEIGHT IS RECORDED TWICE AND DIFFERENTLY: 19 g in the Bone
Summary table, 16 g in the locus description. The count, 13 fragments,
agrees in both. The table value is used here.
THE SLAG SUMMARY'S LOCUS 2 ROW IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: 0 fragments,
100.00% by number, 4 g, 0.00% by weight. Its prose says the majority of
the slag came from Locus 3, while its own table puts 53 of the 62 g in
Locus 1. The count and weight are transcribed as printed; neither the
percentages nor the prose can be reconciled with them.
THE BONE SUMMARY'S PROSE CONTRADICTS ITS TABLE: it says loci 3, 4 and 5
were not excavated and yielded no bone, but the table gives Locus 3 six
fragments weighing 29 g. Loci 4, 5 and 8 are the unexcavated ones.
LOCUS 4'S LENGTH IS 2.70 m ON ITS LOCUS FORM AND SU FORM, AND 2.65 m IN
THE SEASON CONCLUSION. The 2.70 m figure appears twice and is used here.
LOCUS 4 'RISES' 5 cm AT ITS SOUTHWEST VERTEX between opening and closing,
from 23.99 to 24.04, on a feature that was never excavated. Its other
three vertices fall, by 9 cm, 2 cm and 2 cm. These are the same stone tops
measured twice; the spread bounds the repeatability of a plumb bob, line
level and tape at roughly 5 cm on an irregular stone surface.
